strongest_confirmed_findings: Q2 recognized incremental cloud revenue was $1.6B; Q1/Q2 exit nameplate IT draw was 1.0/1.4GW. Period-average total nameplate bounds imply a noncanonical $4.57-$6.40M/MW-year diagnostic, $5.33M base.
SpaceX says nameplate compute draw excludes facility overhead and is not actual consumption or utilization; PUE and canonical effective-utilized-MW economics remain undisclosed.
Financing exposure includes $13.329B related-party Valor failed-sale-leaseback debt, $27.955B consolidated noncancelable commitments and $25B unsecured bonds; do not sum due to perimeter differences.
investable_read_through: Recognized cloud monetization is real and Q2 AI adjusted EBITDA turned positive, but the disclosed revenue/nameplate diagnostic is far below the separate $30-$50M per stated MW-year best guess. Short termination rights, one AI customer at 19.5% of consolidated Q2 revenue and heavy fixed financing make contract durability and cohort payback the key risk variables.
contradictions_to_prior_assumptions: Prior model placeholders of PUE=1 and 100% availability are invalid. The filed nameplate metric is IT load only and expressly not utilization.
The prior capex-only method can now be upgraded to a recognized-revenue diagnostic, but not to canonical effective-MW economics.
unresolved_questions: Which dated MW were externally allocated versus internal, and what was measured physical utilization?
What site/fleet facility and IT energy establish PUE?
Which customer is Customer B, and how do Google/Anthropic/other agreements map to recognized revenue and termination rights?
How does the less-than-one-year payback claim reconcile to cohort capex, cash margin, financing and replacement?
recheck_tonight: Any new 8-K, customer contract exhibit, debt/lease disclosure or Memphis power update after the Q2 filing.
Whether management or counterparties identify Customer B or quantify external MW/utilization.
Whether cloud termination, prepayment, delivery-credit or PPA terms change the durability read.
